title: Serialize pending drain by destination
summary: Serialize pending drain and stale-attempt recovery by canonical final destination and fail duplicate-target manifests into review.
reason: Remediate P1 AUDIT-FIND-W04-005. Per-manifest locks do not protect the shared final media and sidecar destination when distinct manifests name the same server_out.
affected_areas: final media and sidecar reveal rollback
behavior_before: Different manifest files can pass destination checks concurrently and then reveal, verify, or roll back one shared final path under independent locks.
behavior_after: A stable canonical destination lock serializes drain and recovery across processes, manifests are re-read under lock, and duplicate-target manifests fail closed into explicit review before final placement.
tests_added: Two actual drain wrappers in separate PowerShell processes use different manifests and case/separator aliases for one final path; the second fails on the destination lock while exact payload and manifest hashes, sidecar absence, final absence, and zero completion rows remain unchanged.
Two readable manifests targeting one canonical destination both enter review_duplicate_destination without publishing or removing either payload/manifest.
Stale-attempt recovery fails busy without changing manifest, payload, partial, or final state while the destination is locked, then reconciles after release.
Static safety assertions enforce manifest-then-destination lock ordering across drain and recovery and require stable retained lock sentinels.
manual_validation: PowerShell parser accepted pending_transactions.ps1, pending_drain_transaction.ps1, pending_repair.ps1, and both touched pending test scripts.
Invoke-PendingPublishTransactionFaultInjectionChecks.ps1 passed its complete park/drain fault campaign plus destination concurrency, duplicate-target review, and recovery-lock cases.
Pending service/manifest/repair Python slices passed: 19 focused pending manifest/service tests and 40 pending/repair tests with 6 subtests.
Invoke-AdversarialForceKillEncodeChecks.ps1 passed: killed encode was not accepted, source remained queued, and active diagnostics reconciled to interrupted.
Test-WebViewBrowserLargeTableSmoke.ps1 passed one browser test and posted no mutation routes.
Active reliability wrapper passed architecture, native cleanup, runtime-state hygiene, and sidecar safety, then stopped on the known unrelated static WebView assets assertion.
rollback_plan: Revert the destination lock helpers, drain/recovery lock ordering, duplicate-target review guard, tests, generated context, and this packet together. Pending payloads and manifests remain the rollback authority; never delete or overwrite source media.
notes: High-risk Pending Publish boundary reviewed in docs/operator/NO_TOUCH_BOUNDARY_REGISTER.md. Static, disposable two-process, fault-injection, recovery, tool-integration, browser read-only, and adversarial force-kill gates pass. The packet remains in_progress because the boundary register and audit validation rung explicitly require a representative real-media deferred publish to drain pilot before release; no operator-approved representative sample or isolated real-media destination was supplied, and source mutation remains forbidden.
